summary: A GitHub repository poller's read positions (`items_since`, `comments_since`) no longer move past the time the look began. A position took the newest `updated_at` a listing returned. On 2026-11-01, while US Pacific clocks fell back, GitHub stamped some records an hour in the future, and a poller's position jumped to that stamp: every change stamped before it was filtered out of the listings until real time caught up. A position now stops at the look's own start, so a future-stamped record costs at most a re-read. A cursor an earlier build left in the future reads on from the look's start.

replay.detail: No claim or projection replay; changes a poller already skipped are not re-read by this change.

schema.detail: No table, file or schema change; the cursor keeps its shape.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention or digest change.

compatibility.detail: Only the poller's own cursor values change; no claim kind, field or wire capability changes, and an older build reads the same cursor.

recovery.detail: Rolling back restores the old watermark; a future stamp could again hide changes until its time.
